correctness.rationale: All 15 edge weights, graph, budget and quantifiers are explicit. Price-preserving averaging yields an attainable two-class optimum; exact five-mode Fourier decomposition gives the complete spectrum. The derivative numerator D_t is strictly decreasing and changes boundary sign exactly at \(t=2/5\), giving a unique radical-valued maximizer. Equality of Rayleigh quotients across group conjugates forces the original arbitrary allocation to annihilate two Fiedler modes; real/imaginary nodewise equations then force each individual edge deviation to zero. The threshold, both regimes and \(t\to0\) asymptotics have been checked symbolically and by separate exact-rational characteristic-polynomial computations. The standalone checker produced four exact characteristic identities plus 12 full spectra and 720 nonsymmetric comparisons. Finite checks do not prove the continuous theorem; the analytical argument does.

originality.rationale: The narrow assessed contribution is the exact variable-price \(t>0\) Petersen frontier 2/5, unique edgewise optimal allocation on all fifteen independent conductances, and its four-to-five-dimensional Fiedler transition. The equal-price Petersen spectral optimum is already covered (including explicit discrete-time Petersen mixing in 2007 and continuous-time equal-price conformal rigidity in 2024); those subcases are attributed. The 2005 general SDP and 2015 fixed-intralayer two-layer results do not state or imply the claimed heterogeneous-priced closed-form classification. Scoped semantic published-finding corpus and primary-literature searches and statement comparisons found no stronger covering theorem; residual niche-history risk is disclosed.
residual_risks: An unpublished or poorly indexed priced-Petersen conductance optimization may duplicate the exact threshold or uniqueness statement.
Broader graph-design results with directly specializing equal-cost or fixed-layer hypotheses might have unstated corollaries; claims of novelty should be checked by independent bibliographic review.
No exhaustive census of all historical literature or unpublished work is claimed.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical strongly regular ten-vertex testbed, and its price-breaking decomposition into two cycles and a matching is natural in interconnection design. The result determines a sharp rational 2/5 threshold where optimal conductance ratios switch regimes, proves that expensive matching edges cannot be profitably deleted, determines the complete globally unique 15-edge allocation for every price, and reveals a 4-to-5 Fiedler multiplicity transition and cheap-spoke square-root asymptotics. These phenomena are not unweighted spectral-table lookups or tiny numerical gains, and the formulas give an explicit resource-allocation benchmark. No sweeping claims about practical deployment or other graph families are made.
